title: Free-roaming workshop landscape
prompt:
Edit the supplied portfolio mockup image, keeping its spatial arrangement and free-roaming premise, but change the VISUAL STYLE decisively. The current image looks like a photograph of a wooden miniature; that is wrong. Make it look like a finished screenshot from a charming HAND-PAINTED LOW-POLY 3D INDIE GAME. Use simplified chunky faceted objects, broad flat painted material regions, subtly drawn edges, soft graphic contact shadows, almost NO wood grain, no pores, no realistic material roughness or depth of field. The whole world is equally readable. It should look authored and illustrated, not remotely like a real photograph or architectural render. Do NOT add branding, a palette, gradient background, UI cards or marketing phrases.

Keep same landscape: one continuous open irregular tabletop ground, central layered low hill with wide walking ramp, workshop rear left with screen and breadboard, little round-window building rear right with roof accessible by side ramp, small game shed front right, marble track on left, tiny player near bottom center. All buildings and ramps need to be large and wide enough for the tiny player to walk into and around. Turn the rough realistic timber into simple clean toy-like painted plywood with subtle irregular cut edges. Allow unpainted pale wood ground, occasional faded green plank sections, ordinary red electrical wire and cream paper drawings, all intrinsic material colors with no imposed complementary color scheme. Add a few larger illustrated paper trees and simple folded shrubs; reduce incidental clutter. Replace current wind-up bird with a very simple paper-cut bird silhouette. Simplify the background workbench to soft blocky geometry that establishes scale but does not look photorealistic. No dilapidation, tiny grime, fussy wood textures or abandoned ambience. Keep warm daylight rendered as flat friendly game lighting, not cinematic glow.

The little wooden player becomes a simple expressive low-poly carved character with a round wood head, dark jumper, short legs and boots, back-facing. It is a controllable character, not a mascot badge. Camera remains third-person following, pulled back enough to show free traversable space. Make the central ground WIDE and OPEN, not thin walkways between stations. Screens are optional points of interaction, not compulsory teleport stops. No route markers.

Maintain tiny plain text 'Storm Selvig' upper left, 'Index' upper right, controls bottom left 'WASD / arrows — move    Drag — look    E — interact'. Keep the little physical 'Work' sign. No other text. 1536x1024 landscape. The required visual transformation must be obvious: flat painted polygonal game art with readable simplified silhouettes, NOT the same photograph with slightly smoother textures.
initialPrompt:
Create ONE beautifully authored stylized real-time 3D videogame-like screenshot for an explorable personal portfolio website. Desktop landscape 1536x1024. This is a VISUAL MOCKUP, not a corporate website, not a poster. There are no taglines, large titles, header bars, UI cards, colorway swatches, numbered project stations, floating project models, travel hotspots, or destination arrows. The only overlay text is small plain 'Storm Selvig' at top left, 'Index' at top right, and quiet bottom-left controls 'WASD / arrows — move    Drag — look    E — interact'. All text unobtrusive, legible. The world is the entire interface.

Create a single compact playful handmade landscape sitting on a battered everyday wooden workbench. It resembles a miniature game level someone has built from things in their workshop, NOT an abandoned building, NOT a luxury product render, NOT a tropical island and NOT a pop-up book. Art direction: genuinely illustrated three-dimensional objects with slightly irregular low-poly silhouettes, brush-painted surfaces and soft broad baked shadows, a handmade stop-motion videogame feel. Matte materials, visible deliberate brush strokes, simplified geometry, slightly wonky practical construction. Absolutely no photorealism, no excessive microtexture or cinematic grime, no generic smooth clay blobs. Mostly natural plywood and cardboard materials, a few painted muted green panels and the colours of ordinary wires; no imposed designer complementary palette.

Spatial design is crucial: a wide irregular plywood base platform fills the viewport, with lots of continuous OPEN WALKABLE GROUND between three small constructed structures. A subtle rounded ridge at its edge and larger real-sized soldering tools and loose screws beyond it establish miniature scale. The traversable ground has pencil sketches, screw holes, small chips, three pieces of masking tape and a few scratches; do not cover the ground in obstacles. Small ramps and wide gentle steps connect low platforms. You can walk around either side of every structure, move off any implied path, and circle the entire landscape. One central low hill made from layered rounded plywood sheets makes an accessible raised lookout with a long gentle ramp, not a narrow bridge. There is ample walkable ground all around it.

Place an open-sided little workshop toward the back left built from thin plywood, corrugated cardboard roof and a hinged wall; inside a miniature desk with an ordinary screen and a tiny white breadboard with jumper wires (the maker works with embedded electronics). A tiny hand-lettered sign says 'Work'. Back right is a low little timber room with a round window, pinned drawings inside, and a side ramp that lets the player climb onto its flat roof, which connects by a short wide plank to the central raised platform. Far right lower side is a simple smaller open shed with an ordinary screen showing a tiny game, no arcade neon. These are places to enter, not models representing projects. Keep the structures inviting and varied, built by same hands, not identical station kiosks. Real project details would open only on deliberate interaction.

A small original playable character, roughly one doorway tall, stands near bottom center facing into the open ground. The character is a tiny wooden peg-like person with simple boots, a dark knitted jumper, a rounded head and no facial detail; viewed from behind, definitely not a mascot logo. Third-person follow-camera composition, moderately elevated to show the whole landscape and character, approx 35-degree pitch, NOT top-down orthographic or a dollhouse product shot. Scattered small playful details that do not gate progress: a marble beside a low wood track, a wind-up bird on a roof, a tiny movable stool. One little ramp passes UNDER an accessible roof creating a loop route. No quest markers, scores, collectible trails or forced route. No arrows or connection lines. No splash screens or central start button. Have a coherent open space with many reachable viewpoints and visual landmarks. Do not put a huge computer or giant mechanical clock in the middle. World should feel curious, crafted, playful and inviting, more like an indie game environment than photoreal architecture. Large readable spatial forms, a completely new particular composition, enough texture and personal construction detail to avoid template/AI portfolio aesthetics. Everything is part of one continuous reachable free-roaming space.
notes: Approved by the user on 2026-10-27. Visual reference for the implemented free-roaming miniature workshop; the image itself is a generated concept, not a runtime screenshot.
